title: Class actions
summary: A class action allows named parties to litigate on behalf of an adequately defined group of absent persons when the requirements for representative litigation are satisfied. It can make small claims viable and resolve common issues together.
notes: A large number of similar claims does not alone justify certification. The full chapter includes both access benefits and risks to absent members or defendants.

sections.Meaning: A class action allows named parties to litigate on behalf of an adequately defined group of absent persons when the requirements for representative litigation are satisfied. It can make small claims viable and resolve common issues together.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the class and representatives. Apply Rule 23(a)’s prerequisites and a category under Rule 23(b). Then address notice, opt-out rights, representation, jurisdiction, settlement if proposed, and the scope of any binding judgment.
